title: Multimodal digital biomarker for asthma: complementary roles of vocal, clinical and demographic factors
desc: Asthma affects over 260 million people worldwide, yet diagnosis remains dependent on spirometry and specialist assessment, limiting accessibility in primary care and low-resource settings. Vocal biomarkers offer a promising non-invasive alternative, but prior studies have largely focused on acoustic features without integrating clinical context. We present a multimodal Mixture-of-Experts framework for asthma identification that adaptively combines acoustic embeddings from sustained vowel phonation and reading passage tasks with structured clinical and demographic data. The model was evaluated on a matched cohort of 1218 self-reported asthma cases and healthy controls from the Colive Voice study. The multimodal model achieved an AUROC of 0.83 and Brier score of 0.18, outperforming unimodal approaches. Exploratory analysis of the gating mechanism in asthma cases showed that greater respiratory symptom burden was associated with increased weighting of reading-passage modality and reduced weighting of sustained-vowel phonation modality. These findings support the feasibility of voice-based identification of self-reported asthma; however, independent prospective validation remains necessary before clinical use.

title: DAF: Deterministic affinity-guided latent flow for flexible many-to-many multiphase liver MRI synthesis
desc: Publication date: February 2027 Source: Medical Image Analysis, Volume 116 Author(s): Shunjie Dong, Yulin Pu, Zhehan Shen, Xueyang Zou, Lin Deng, Chengyan Wang, Guangtao Xue, Xingfeng Shao, Ruokun Li

title: Liquid biopsy and cancer therapy: current technology, diagnosis, prognosis, and cancer treatments.
desc: [Molecular biomedicine] Liquid biopsy offers repeated, minimally invasive molecular profiling of cancer, but its clinical value depends on the analyte, analytical platform, and intended use. In this Review, we evaluate current liquid-biopsy technologies for diagnosis, prognosis, and treatment guidance, with a particular emphasize on tumor-derived extracellular vesicles (TDEVs) as a bridge between biomarker detection and therapeutic intervention. We examine genomic and epigenomic profiling, single-cell and single-vesicle analysis, and multi-omics integration as complementary approaches for assessing tumour burden, heterogeneity and treatment response. Circulating tumor DNA genotyping guides targeted therapy in selected advanced cancers, whereas many early-detection and vesicle-based applications require prospective validation. We highlight how the TDEV lipid bilayer protects diverse molecular cargo that reflects evolving tumour phenotypes and how TDEV-mediated communication contributes to metastasis, immune evasion and therapeutic resistance, creating opportunities to target pathogenic vesicle signalling. We also assess engineered vesicles from malignant and non-malignant cells as drug-delivery and cancer-vaccination platforms, while noting that tumour-derived carriers may retain oncogenic or immunosuppressive cargo. Most candidate vesicle biomarkers remain supported by retrospective studies, and therapeutic platforms are largely preclinical or in early clinical testing. We discuss the requirements for clinical translation, including reliable identification of tumour-derived vesicles, standardized workflows and prospective multicentre validation for diagnostics, and reproducible manufacturing, cargo characterization, potency testing and product-specific pharmacokinetic and safety evaluation for therapeutics. Finally, we consider how multimodal profiling and artificial intelligence might improve signal integration, and argue that clinical adoption will depend on demonstrating that vesicle-guided decisions and interventions improve patient outcomes.

title: LesionAgent: Training-Free Agentic Tumor Tracking and Response Assessment in Longitudinal CT
desc: Every few months, a cancer patient's CT scans decide whether treatment continues. 3D foundation models can now detect, segment, register and track lesions, yet none of them reads the scans as a radiologist does. A radiologist decides which findings are lesions, which are the same lesion months later and whether a new spot means progression, and checks each decision against the extensive rules of a clinical guideline. We introduce LesionAgent, an LLM agent that performs this read end to end without task-specific training. It operates frozen 3D models as tools, acts in 3D through coordinate-labelled views, remembers every lesion across visits in a registry, verifies every model output it relies on, and leaves every number to a deterministic guideline engine. On four public longitudinal CT datasets, LesionAgent tracks more lesions and measures them more accurately than every automatic basel

title: MicroBioAgent: an AI agent for automated microbiome analysis
desc: Microbiome data analysis demands customized workflows tailored to specific biological questions, sequencing modalities, and data properties. However, constructing and executing these workflows requires navigating heterogeneous software dependencies, reference databases, and multi-step parameter tuning. Here, we present MicroBioAgent, an autonomous, domain-specific agent framework that translates high-level biological queries into executable, study-specific pipelines across 16S rRNA amplicon, reference-based shotgun, and de novo assembly-based metagenomics. Rather than relying on static pipeline templates, MicroBioAgent employs a closed-loop execution architecture: it dynamically selects and runs bioinformatics tools within user-controlled environments while iteratively inspecting intermediate outputs to adapt downstream analytical decisions. Furthermore, to address the long-running nature of metagenomic computation, we introduce an asynchronous background task-management mechanism that reduces LLM token consumption by over 50% while enabling real-time plan adjustment and automated workflow resumption. We systematically evaluated MicroBioAgent across three benchmarks of increasing complexity: (1) paired amplicon and shotgun profiling of tomato rhizosphere microbiomes, (2) taxonomic and functional profiling coupled with machine-learning classification in a colorectal cancer cohort, and (3) de novo metagenomic assembly, metagenome-assembled genome (MAG) binning, and metabolic pathway reconstruction in a polyethylene degradation study. Across all benchmarks, MicroBioAgent faithfully recapitulated the primary biological findings of the original studies, exhibiting high analytical concordance despite expected tool- and database-dependent variations. In systematic robustness evaluations across 27 independent runs spanning three backbone large language models and three prompt-complexity tiers, MicroBioAgent achieved a 98.8% task completion rate and yielded highly reproducible diversity and differential-abundance estimates. MicroBioAgent establishes a scalable, adaptive paradigm for end-to-end computational microbiome research.

From Data to Discovery: Machine Learning-Driven Integration of Multi-Omics Data in Oncology.
source: PubMed · Methods in molecular biology (Clifton, N.J.)
desc: [Methods in molecular biology (Clifton, N.J.)] Multi-omics integration amalgamates genomic, transcriptomic, epigenomic, and proteomic layers to provide a systems-level portrait of multifaceted diseases such as cancer. However, its practical application faces constraints posed by challenges including elevated dimensionality, diverse data types, and prevalent missing values. This review delivers a structured summary of recent advances in machine-learning-driven integration of multi-omics datasets, with a specific emphasis on the potential of this field for translational cancer research. First, we discuss the importance of multi-omics integration. Next, we provide an overview of key machine learning methodologies, including high-dimensional variable selection techniques (e.g., knockoff filters for controlling the false discovery rate), deep learning models (for survival prediction and classification), and generative models (e.g., diffusion models and variational autoencoders for data augmentation and missing data imputation). These approaches demonstrate high accuracy in cancer subtype classification, biomarker discovery, prognosis evaluation, and personalized therapy. For example, they achieve over 85% accuracy in triple-negative breast cancer subtype analysis. We also cover the contributions of single-cell multi-omics technologies (e.g., SHARE-seq and SNARE-seq) and emerging databases (e.g., scImmOmics and scCancerExplorer) to enhancing data resolution. While challenges remain in terms of interpretability and computational efficiency, integrating explainable AI and multimodal learning shows promise in accelerating clinical translation. This review seeks to equip researchers with a systematic methodological roadmap and demonstrate its practical utility in precision medicine via exemplar case studies.

title: Scalable Evaluation of Medical AI using Evidence-based Practice Recommendations
desc: Rigorously evaluating medical artificial intelligence (AI) requires testing open-ended clinical management across diverse presentations and stages of care. However, existing benchmarks rely on manual expert authoring, limiting coverage across conditions, conditional care pathways, and evolving guidelines. We develop an automated pipeline that extracts and verifies structured clinical criteria and branching decision trees from practice recommendations to generate scenarios spanning the care continuum, including nuanced presentations and practice variations across regions and guideline editions. Applied to 436 BMJ Best Practice clinical monographs (354 US, 82 International), this yields 3,200 scenarios spanning differential diagnosis, investigations, treatment, and complications, plus targeted suites for regional specificity (731 US/International pairs) and temporal freshness (630 scenario

title: An open long non-coding RNA foundation model for generalizable prediction
desc: Long non-coding RNAs (lncRNAs) play essential roles in transcriptional regulation and chromatin organization, yet predicting their functional properties from sequence remains challenging because informative signals span both local motifs and long-range base pairing across kilobase-scale transcripts. Current RNA foundation models are restricted to short sequences and existing lncRNA prediction models narrowly focus on isolated tasks, leaving a dedicated foundation model notably absent. Here we present LncRFM, a dedicated lncRNA foundation model, supported by the LncCorpus pretraining data and the LncBench evaluation suite, which stand for a systematic framework to decode lncRNAs. For foundation model pretraining, we develop a hybrid bidirectional state-space encoder trained with a structure-guided masking strategy to effectively capture both local sequence patterns and long-range contexts. For pretraining data, we contribute over 9.6 million lncRNA sequences to assemble LncCorpus, a pretraining corpus of 24.7 million sequences. For benchmarking evaluation, we construct a comprehensive benchmark, LncBench, comprising 15 datasets and totaling over 1,010,000 sequences across 10 prediction tasks: six core lncRNA functional and annotation tasks and four structural and regulatory RNA assay tasks. Evaluated against seven RNA foundation models under a unified frozen-encoder protocol, our LncRFM achieves the state-of-the-art primary-metric scores on 11 of the 13 datasets that allow downstream adaptation. On two external generalization benchmarks evaluated without further adaptation, LncRFM matches the best structure-specialized baseline in F1 (0.141) and achieves the highest AUROC (0.962) on lncRNA contact prediction, while maintaining competitive cross-species coding-potential transfer (F1 of 0.374) under severe multi-kingdom domain shift. To benefit the scientific community, we make all datasets, source code, and pretrained models publicly available.

title: From eminence to evidence to intelligence-based medicine: optimising artificial intelligence to disrupt dogma in emergency departments.
desc: [Frontiers in public health] The evolution of medical epistemology from the unassailable authority of eminence to the empirical rigour of evidence has prepared the healthcare system for its most profound transformation yet, intelligence-based medicine. Driven by the integration of artificial intelligence (AI), this emerging era offers unprecedented capabilities to process complex health data and personalise patient care within high-stakes environments like emergency departments. However, this paradigm shift simultaneously introduces a critical risk of modernised, digital dogma, manifesting as algorithmic paternalism. If AI systems are deployed without rigorous oversight, they threaten to silently amplify historical biases, diagnostic inaccuracies, and outdated clinical heuristics, trading the unquestioned authority of historical figures for the presumed infallibility of machines. To safeguard care in emergency departments, AI must not operate unchecked. Adapting existing Learning Health System frameworks offers a pragmatic solution to govern AI integration. By embedding these computational technologies within continuous, self-correcting clinical ecosystems, departments can enforce robust data hygiene and rigorously audit data provenance. An essential component of this approach is separating objective safety surveillance and adverse event reporting from the algorithm's internal learning mechanisms to detect epistemic drift and automation bias. Ultimately, the successful and safe integration of intelligence-based medicine depends on an unwavering commitment to transparent governance. When computational power is harnessed as a regulated, transparent tool within an LHS, AI can actively dismantle entrenched clinical dogma, ensuring future care is anchored in dynamic, validated evidence rather than perpetuating the medical errors propagated by eminence from the past.

title: Evidence sufficiency assessment enables cost-effective review allocation in on-premise clinical AI agents
desc: On-premise clinical AI agents must auto-accept high-confidence diagnoses, deferring others to clinician review, yet token probabilities and self-reported confidence miss errors, while more reliable five-run consistency incurs fivefold compute. We propose training-free decision-point evidence sufficiency assessment and a three-tier sequential triage protocol. Masking reasoning and diagnosis, the same 4B model scores sufficiency from objective evidence via prior-debiased probabilities over five ordered levels. Calibration freezes a nominal top-50% threshold, selecting single-run, five-run consistency, or full-deferral tiers by whether the one-sided 95% Wilson lower confidence bound of pass rate among accepted cases meets the 95% clinical target line. Across 1,605 MIRA-v2, CDM, VivaBench, and in-hospital liver malignancy primary cohort cases, MIRA-v2 single-run top-50% pass rate reached 98.

title: Machine learning and deep learning for predicting acute exacerbation in chronic obstructive pulmonary disease: a systematic review.
desc: [Systematic reviews] Acute exacerbation of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (AECOPD) imposes a substantial burden on patients and healthcare systems. Although traditional risk assessment tools exist, machine learning (ML) and deep learning (DL) may offer improved prediction. This systematic review aims to evaluate the performance of ML and DL algorithms for predicting AECOPD risk. This review was conducted in accordance with the PRISMA guidelines. PubMed, Embase, Cochrane Library and Web of Science were systematically searched from 1 January 2021 to 6 May 2026. Studies that developed or validated ML and DL models for predicting AECOPD risk were included. Methodological quality, risk of bias and applicability were assessed using the PROBAST + AI, and reporting quality was assessed using the TRIPOD + AI. Because of substantial heterogeneity, we synthesised model performance descriptively. Thirteen studies were included, of which only two performed external validation. Overall, reported AUC values ranged widely from 0.661 to 0.9721. By outcome type, AUC values for AECOPD risk prediction ranged from 0.668 to 0.9721, whereas those for AECOPD‑related hospitalisation ranged from 0.661 to 0.885. Similarly, by prediction windows, short‑term prediction achieved AUCs of 0.668‑0.972, compared with 0.661‑0.884 for long‑term prediction. However, PROBAST + AI revealed high methodological quality concerns and risk of bias in all 13 studies, and TRIPOD + AI showed suboptimal reporting transparency with an overall completeness rate of 54.3%. Limited evidence indicates that models for any AECOPD may outperform those for hospitalisation, and that models with shorter prediction windows may show higher AUCs, although this association could be confounded by small sample sizes and potential patient-level leakage. These findings provide valuable direction for future model development and validation, although the current evidence base is constrained by methodological quality concerns, risk of bias and suboptimal reporting transparency. PROSPERO CRD420261391432.

title: Leakage-Free Is Not Confounder-Free: What a Patient-Level Split Cannot Certify About a Medical Imaging Benchmark
desc: Patient-level splitting is the standard safeguard against subject leakage in medical imaging evaluation, but it cannot remove a confounder that every fold inherits: an acquisition variable aligned with the diagnosis across the whole cohort. We present a five-question audit of a candidate confounder: how well it predicts the diagnosis, whether it can be decoded from the images, whether diagnostic scores depend on it, whether the image adds predictive value beyond it and how much discrimination survives once it is controlled. We apply it to DMR-IR, the public dataset on which most machine-learning results in breast thermography rest. From Gene Sets to Brain Function: A Physiology-Informed Framework for Multi-Omics Integration in Precision Neurophysiology.
source: PubMed · Chronic diseases and translational medicine
desc: [Chronic diseases and translational medicine] Public omics repositories and multi-omics technologies have substantially expanded the molecular characterization of chronic human diseases by enabling large-scale analyses across diverse biological and clinical contexts. However, in neurological disorders, translating omics-derived associations into mechanistic insight and clinical relevance remains challenging due to the dynamic and multiscale nature of brain function. Gene set-based analytical approaches effectively identify enriched molecular patterns, but are limited in capturing temporal dynamics, network-level interactions, and physiological state dependence that define neural systems. This conceptual methodological review synthesizes foundational infrastructure papers, methodological evaluations, and translational neuroscience literature to critically examine the application of public omics resources in human neurophysiology, focusing on the interpretive gap between molecular-level associations and functional brain processes. We examine major public omics infrastructures, widely used gene set analysis frameworks, the principal strategies for multi-omics integration, and the challenge of batch effects in public data reuse, highlighting both their analytical strengths and structural limitations. Core neurophysiological principles, including synaptic transmission, network dynamics, plasticity, and homeostatic regulation, are discussed to clarify why direct inference from static molecular profiles to brain function is inherently constrained. Clinical illustrations from epilepsy, attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder, and migraine demonstrate how chronic neurological disorders emerge from context-dependent neural dynamics that are not readily reducible to gene set-level summaries. Finally, we outline future directions for integrating artificial intelligence with public omics resources, emphasizing physiology-informed modeling, explainable AI, and ethical considerations to support more interpretable and translational precision health strategies in chronic neurological disease.

title: Observed, Curated, Reused: Observation Bias in Clinical AI Evaluation
desc: Clinical AI evaluations are vulnerable to observation bias embedded in routine medical documentation, which captures only what clinicians notice, test, and record rather than a complete clinical picture. As this evidence travels into publications and reference knowledge graphs, crucial distinctions disappear: unexamined symptoms blur with confirmed negatives, and chronological disease progression is lost. Surviving evidence can also enter both the benchmark query and the reference knowledge base, creating a self-referential loop where a patient is evaluated against clues derived from their own published case report. To quantify this bias, we tracked 6,503 clinical cases across six historical Human Phenotype Ontology (HPO) releases (October 2021-June 2026) to identify when HPO first cited the publications describing them. Artificial Intelligence in Thoracic Pathology and Biomarker Assessment: An IASLC Pathology Committee Review.
source: PubMed · Journal of thoracic oncology : official publication of the International Association for the Study of Lung Cancer
desc: [Journal of thoracic oncology : official publication of the International Association for the Study of Lung Cancer] Artificial intelligence (AI) is starting to transform pathology by enhancing diagnostic accuracy, prognostication, and therapeutic prediction through advanced computational analysis of histopathological images. This review explores key AI methodologies and their applications in lung cancer diagnostics. Supervised learning dominates current clinical AI tools, relying on annotated whole-slide images (WSIs) for tasks like tumor subtyping, quantitation of tissue-based parameters, prediction of driver alterations (e.g. EGFR and KRAS mutations, ALK rearrangement), and assessment of tumor microenvironment (TME) features. Meanwhile, weakly supervised and self-supervised learning (SSL) methods, such as multiple instance learning (MIL) and contrastive learning, reduce dependency on labor-intensive annotations and uncover novel prognostic morphologic patterns. AI demonstrates strong performance in predicting therapeutic responses, including immune checkpoint inhibitor efficacy and pathologic response to neoadjuvant therapy, while emerging techniques like spatial transcriptomics and multiplex immunofluorescence further leverage AI to decode complex spatial biology and generate novel biomarkers. Despite much progress, major challenges persist in validation, reliability, interpretability, regulatory approval, ethics and data privacy standards, cost and reimbursement, equity, and integration into clinical workflows. Adoption requires scalable digital pathology infrastructure, interdisciplinary collaboration, and suitable reimbursement frameworks. Regulatory efforts aim to address ethical and safety concerns, but global harmonization remains incomplete. We also consider the professional consequences of adoption, including cognitive deskilling, workforce displacement, and the conditions under which pathologist oversight remains meaningful rather than nominal, and argue that liability should follow the reality of control. As AI evolves, particularly with foundation models and large language models (LLMs), thoracic pathology stands to benefit from substantially extended diagnostic and predictive capabilities, pending resolution of implementation barriers.

title: Neurodegenerative Differential Diagnosis with Knowledge-enhanced Structural Reasoning
desc: Accurate differential diagnosis of neurodegenerative disorders remains challenging due to overlapping clinical manifestations and heterogeneous, often incomplete multimodal observations. Existing multimodal models can integrate imaging and clinical measurements but often overlook disease-specific evidence patterns and pairwise relations among competing diagnoses. We therefore propose Knowledge-enhanced Structural Reasoning (KnowSR), which aligns multimodal patient representations with a literature-grounded knowledge bank of disease prototypes, signed evidence directions, and pairwise diagnostic relations. Deep Learning for Generating Computational PIN-4 Immunohistochemistry Staining from Prostate Biopsy H&E Images.
source: PubMed · Proceedings of the ... International Conference on Machine Learning and Applications. International Conference on Machine Learning and Applications
desc: [Proceedings of the ... International Conference on Machine Learning and Applications. International Conference on Machine Learning and Applications] Immunohistochemistry (IHC) staining is frequently used to resolve diagnostically ambiguous prostate cancer biopsy findings on hematoxylin and eosin (H&E)-stained tissue. However, PIN-4 IHC is typically performed on adjacent tissue sections, limiting direct spatial comparison between the H&E morphology that indicated the need for IHC and the corresponding immunophenotypic signal. A paired, registered H&E/PIN-4 dataset was constructed from routine clinical prostate biopsy whole-slide images (WSIs), and a conditional generative adversarial network (cGAN) was trained to synthesize PIN-4 staining patterns directly from native H&E image patches. The final dataset comprised 172 paired WSIs from 93 patients and 27,298 registered 1024 × 1024 patch pairs, spanning adenocarcinoma-positive and benign cases with representation across age, race, and ethnicity groups. The model was evaluated on an independent held-out test set of 1,814 patch pairs from 17 WSIs, achieving a mean peak signal-to-noise ratio (PSNR) of 21.88 dB, structural similarity index measure (SSIM) of 0.667, Pearson correlation coefficient (PCC) of 0.684, and learned perceptual image patch similarity (LPIPS) of 0.417. Qualitative review by a board-certified pathologist demonstrated that generated images captured diagnostically relevant PIN-4 staining patterns, including AMACR/racemase expression and basal-cell-associated staining, while preserving spatial correspondence with the source H&E morphology. Synthesis quality varied across morphologically complex regions, including high-grade carcinoma and intraductal carcinoma. These results support the feasibility of supervised computational PIN-4 staining from routinely acquired brightfield H&E prostate biopsy images. The approach enables direct interpretation of predicted PIN-4 marker patterns in the context of the source prostate H&E architecture, addressing a current spatial limitation of conventional adjacent-section IHC.

title: BioELX: Context-Aware Cross-lingual Biomedical Entity Linking without Task-Specific Supervision
desc: Cross-lingual biomedical entity linking (BEL) maps mentions in any language to unique identifiers in a biomedical knowledge base, supporting clinical and biomedical NLP applications. We identify two issues affecting current systems. First, the UMLS (Bodenreider,2004) aliases used to train cross-lingual BEL retrievers are heavily skewed toward English, so retrievers generalize poorly to non-English mentions. Second, although context is often necessary for disambiguation, naively injecting context into retrievers trained only to align aliases severely degrades retrieval. We propose BioELX, a retrieve-rerank framework that addresses both issues. For retrieval, we continue training SapBERT_multi (Liu et al., 2021b) using Wikidata-derived cross-lingual alias supervision, forming shared concept neighborhoods across languages. Tumor-draining lymph nodes as candidate sources of immunotherapy biomarkers in breast cancer: a multi-omics and artificial intelligence roadmap.
desc: [Biomarker research] Although immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) have transformed breast cancer treatment, predicting durable clinical benefit remains challenging. Current biomarkers, primarily derived from tumor tissue or peripheral blood, do not directly capture the adaptive immune response at its site of initiation. Tumor-draining lymph nodes (TDLNs) are not passive conduits for metastasis but dynamic immunological hubs where anti-tumor T cell priming and immune evasion converge. In this review, we critically examine the nascent intersection of TDLN immunobiology, high-resolution multi-omics, and artificial intelligence (AI) to evaluate TDLN-derived features as candidate next-generation biomarkers for immunotherapy. We synthesize the complex cellular and molecular architecture of the breast cancer TDLN, including T cell exhaustion, B cell-mediated immunity, and stromal crosstalk, before evaluating the state-of-the-art single-cell and spatial technologies capable of decoding this microenvironment. We assess the application of AI and foundation models in this domain, identifying a major methodological gap: while AI frameworks are increasingly mature for primary tumors, their application to TDLNs remains unvalidated and limited by a severe scarcity of annotated multi-omics datasets. Furthermore, we address pivotal translational considerations, including the immunological implications of axillary surgery in the ICI era. We emphasize that no TDLN-derived biomarker has yet undergone prospective validation as a predictive biomarker for immunotherapy in breast cancer, and that retrospective analyses of trial specimens must account for the timing of tissue acquisition relative to systemic therapy. Finally, we chart immediate research priorities, including establishing TDLN reference atlases and developing clinically feasible specimen collection pathways for biomarker validation. This review provides a conceptual framework and translational roadmap to assess whether TDLN-derived features can complement existing tumor-centric metrics in guiding immunotherapy decisions.

title: SecretAgent: A Multi-Agent Framework for Privacy Protection against Vision Language Models
desc: Vision-language models (VLMs) can infer private information from shared images, including locations, personally identifiable information (PII), and personal attributes such as age and sex, even from medical images. Adversarial perturbations can protect such information against black-box VLMs, but existing methods overlook image quality and introduce visible artifacts into the images they protect. We present SecretAgent, the first general multi-agent framework that protects image privacy against VLMs while preserving visual fidelity. LLM agents iteratively locate the visual evidence that reveals private information and adapt an invisible perturbation to the target VLM's answers and to an appearance reviewer agent, which rejects any candidate with visible artifacts. Large Language Model-Assisted Cleaning of Report-Derived Labels in a Large-Scale Chest CT Dataset.
desc: [Journal of medical systems] To evaluate whether large language model (LLM)-assisted label cleaning can identify label-report discordance in CT-RATE, a large-scale public chest CT dataset. After report-level deduplication, 24,446 unique radiology reports from 20,209 unique patients were identified. Twelve reports were excluded from the primary GPT-5.4 analysis because of persistent content-safety filtering or unparsable output, leaving 24,434 reports and 439,812 label instances across 18 abnormality categories. GPT-5.4-derived binary labels were generated from report text using structured outputs and compared with the original CT-RATE labels. Discordant instances were adjudicated by radiologists. In addition, 100 randomly sampled reports were manually annotated as a development set to compare the original CT-RATE labels, individual LLM-derived labels, and three-LLM majority-vote labels against radiologist-annotated reference labels. These label sources were then evaluated against a prespecified, stratified confirmatory set of 250 reports independently annotated by two blinded radiologists, and run-to-run consistency was assessed by repeated runs. Overall agreement between GPT-5.4-derived and CT-RATE labels was 96.4%, with a Cohen's κ of 0.884. Lymphadenopathy showed the lowest agreement and κ. In the confirmatory set (pre-consensus inter-reader κ = 0.936), the majority vote achieved an unweighted label-macro-averaged F1 score of 95.6% and κ of 0.940, compared with 90.8% and 0.879 for the original labels (paired F1 difference, + 4.8 points; 95% CI, 3.6-6.2), and each individual LLM also outperformed the original labels. The instance-level flip rate across three repeated runs was 1.02% for the majority vote. LLM-assisted label cleaning identified substantial label-report discordance in CT-RATE, particularly for lymphadenopathy, and may provide a scalable approach to quality improvement of public imaging datasets. The refined report-aligned labels and associated code will be made publicly available upon acceptance. Because all labels were derived from report text, they reflect report alignment rather than image-level truth.

title: Ruby: State-of-the-Art Potency Prediction across Discovery Regimes Using Learned Structural Representations
desc: Small-molecule drug discovery proceeds through repeated design-make-test-analyze cycles. The goal is often to maximize potency while keeping other properties within the ranges required for a viable therapeutic candidate. Compound prioritization places different demands on computational methods as drug discovery progresses from hit identification through hit-to-lead and lead optimization, with changing computational budgets and increasing amounts of on-target experimental data. We introduce Ruby, a Robust Universal Binding affinitY predictor that uses intermediate representations from the structural foundation model Pearl without requiring an explicit binding pose for every compound. Ruby is trained on proprietary data plus GenesisPotency-2026, an audited public-source potency training dataset released for academic and commercial use under a CC BY-SA 4.0 license with row-level provenance

Unraveling the Shaping of the Microenvironment in Brain Metastasis: From Dissemination to Overt Lesions.
desc: [Cancer communications (London, England)] Brain metastasis (BrM) is a devastating complication of solid tumors, especially melanoma, breast, and lung cancers, and is often associated with a period of latency. The development of BrM is a highly inefficient, multistep process in which disseminated tumor cells must reach the cerebral vasculature after surviving in circulation, traverse the blood-brain barrier (BBB), and then adapt to the specialized neural microenvironment, evade immune surveillance, and instigate a reconfiguration of the microenvironment at the metastatic site to establish a clinically overt metastatic lesion. Increasing evidence has therefore shifted the field from a predominantly cancer cell-centric view toward an integrated model in which metastatic progression depends on continuous reciprocal interactions between tumor cells and the brain microenvironment. In this review, we examine BrM through different stages of the metastatic cascade, from intravasation and vascular dissemination to cerebral arrest, extravasation, dormancy, immune evasion, and metastatic outgrowth. We discuss how cancer cells acquire properties that facilitate their interaction with the cerebral vasculature and how tumor-derived factors remodel the BBB endothelial cells and other components of the metastatic niche. We further highlight the dynamic roles of astrocytes, microglia, infiltrating macrophages, natural killer cells, neutrophils, and other immune populations, which initially restrict metastatic establishment but become progressively reprogrammed to support immune evasion and survival of the metastatic cells and then also help in tumor expansion. Beyond immune and stromal remodeling, emerging studies reveal extensive metabolic and neuronal adaptation within BrM, including altered glucose, lipid, amino acid, and neurotransmitter utilization, as well as direct exploitation of neuronal signaling and synaptic communication. Together, these findings establish the brain metastatic niche as a dynamic ecosystem that is actively remodeled throughout disease progression rather than a passive site of secondary tumor growth. We also discuss advances in BrM detection and therapeutic development, including artificial intelligence-based approaches, and highlight the need for spatially and temporally resolved models that integrate tumor, vascular, immune, glial, neuronal, and metabolic programs to identify stage-specific vulnerabilities and improve BrM prevention and treatment.

title: Learning 3D MRI Representations with Generative Adversarial Networks
desc: Learning representations of visual images is a challenging task. It requires extracting abstract patterns from high-dimensional data without explicit supervision. This becomes pronounced with 3D MR imaging due to sparse features, higher dimensional inputs, and smaller datasets. Many state-of-the-art representation learning algorithms successfully rely on transformers and diffusion-based architectures. However, these methods struggle with smaller datasets. In effect, solution methods relax the problem by slicing 3D volumes and solving the problem for 2D medical imaging, resulting in a loss of spatial 3D information. We present R2RG, a representation learning method based on Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs), with Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) honing the reconstruction task. Our key insights lie in exploiting architectural biases in 3D CNNs, combined with data-efficient auto-en

title: Medtronic (MDT) Won FDA Clearance For Hugo In 3.5 Million US Surgeries
AI and algorithmic literacy among nurses: a concept analysis.
desc: [BMC nursing] To clarify the concept of AI and algorithmic literacy among nurses and to provide a conceptual foundation for nursing education, clinical practice, and responsible AI governance. Rodgers' evolutionary concept analysis. Guided by Rodgers' evolutionary method, the literature was analyzed to determine how AI and algorithmic literacy among nurses has been used and conceptualized. Defining attributes, antecedents, consequences, and related concepts were extracted, compared, and synthesized. A systematic search was conducted in Web of Science, PubMed, Embase, and CINAHL. Search terms focused on nurses, nursing students, health workers, artificial intelligence literacy, algorithmic literacy, AI competence, AI readiness, and generative AI literacy. Articles published between January 2020 and June 2026 were screened. Twenty-eight articles were included in the final concept analysis. Four defining attributes were identified: conceptual understanding of AI-mediated nursing contexts; critical interpretation and risk recognition of algorithmic outputs; clinical integration and human oversight of AI recommendations; and ethical governance awareness grounded in professional accountability. Antecedents included AI education and training, digital or informatics foundations, prior AI exposure, individual readiness, organizational support, faculty preparedness, and governance environments. Consequences included improved learning outcomes, critical thinking, AI adoption and readiness, patient safety awareness, human-AI collaboration, and professional innovation. Related concepts included AI literacy, algorithmic literacy, digital literacy, nursing informatics competence, AI readiness, AI competence, and AI self-efficacy. Based on this synthesis, both a brief definition and a full conceptual definition of AI and algorithmic literacy among nurses were proposed. AI and algorithmic literacy among nurses is a multidimensional concept that extends beyond technical knowledge or willingness to use AI. It reflects nurses' ability to understand, interpret, supervise, and responsibly integrate AI outputs into nursing judgment while maintaining patient safety and professional accountability. Clarifying this concept can support the development of nursing AI education, competency frameworks, measurement tools, clinical training, and governance strategies. As AI becomes increasingly embedded in nursing practice, nurses should be positioned not merely as end users of AI systems but as profes

title: DermKG: A Concept-Centric Knowledge Graph for Interpretable Skin Disease Diagnosis from Dermatological Morphology
desc: Dermatologists describe lesions with a standardized morphological lexicon, which makes concept-based models attractive for interpretable skin disease diagnosis. How much diagnostic information these concepts actually carry, however, is rarely quantified. We present DermKG, a concept-centric knowledge graph built on the expert-annotated SkinCon subset of Fitzpatrick17k (3,230 images, 48 concepts, 113 diseases). DermKG has 3,452 nodes of 8 types and 19,365 edges of 11 relation types, and encodes disease concept profiles, concept co-occurrence, a three-level diagnostic hierarchy, and 20 clinical morphology rules, all of which are supported by the training data (15 strong, 5 moderate). An information-ceiling analysis shows that the 3,230 lesions collapse onto only 813 distinct concept vectors, bounding concept-only top-1 accuracy at 38.9\% for diseases and 77.6\% for the nine categories. Wit

title: Insights into Channelopathies and Sport: The Genotype-Positive/Phenotype-Negative Athlete from Molecular Diagnosis to Management.
desc: [Sports medicine (Auckland, N.Z.)] Channelopathies, diseases with ion channel perturbations, are a major cause of sudden cardiac death in athletes. Advances in genetic testing have identified a growing population of athletes carrying (likely) pathogenic variants in cardiac ion channel genes who remain phenotypically silent. These genotype-positive/phenotype-negative (G+/P-) individuals present a distinct clinical challenge. Standard preparticipation screening, designed around phenotypic findings, provides little guidance for their management. A critical gap exists in providing prognostic guidance based on the involved gene, specific variants, and its molecular consequences. Beyond a critical review of existing literature, we provide a mechanistically anchored framework for variant-specific arrhythmic risk stratification across the major channelopathy genes. For each gene, we translate molecular pathophysiology into clinically actionable risk profiles and examine how exercise-specific triggers, including adrenergic surge, electrolyte shifts, and sympathovagal imbalance, interact with the underlying molecular substrate to modulate arrhythmic vulnerability. Standard diagnostic tools ranging from electro- and echocardiography, exercise stress testing, and pharmacological provocation to emerging modalities such as electroanatomic mapping and magnetocardiography are evaluated for their capacity to unmask subclinical disease and refine sports eligibility decisions. The case for an interdisciplinary sports-cardio-genetic board is made alongside a call for international collaborative registries, as existing evidence in G+/P- athletes is largely absent. The integration of artificial intelligence and telemonitoring into longitudinal athletic surveillance is discussed as a pragmatic strategy for early phenotype detection. Ultimately, guidance for the G+/P- athlete rests on a thorough understanding of the causative genetic variant and its pathophysiological consequences.

title: Embodied-Harness: Towards Recursive Self-Improvement for Robotic Manipulation
desc: Vision-language model (VLM)-based agents offer a promising approach to robotic manipulation, yet remain limited by inadequate memory organization, uncertain failure attribution, and limited reuse of execution experience. We propose Embodied-Harness, a dual-agent framework that improves manipulation by refining the execution harness without updating model parameters. The Actor interacts with the environment through a robot-control interface, while the Reflector converts execution evidence into reusable operational guidance. Hierarchical Memory Architecture maintains short-term execution context and long-term experiential knowledge to support execution and reflection. Evidence-based Experience Reflection grounds failure diagnosis in observed interactions, while Recursive Harness Self-Improvement refines operational guidance across successive attempts. Experiments on RoboTwin 2.0, RoboSPA,

title: Evaluating the Accuracy of an Artificial Intelligence Solution Program for Identifying Anatomical Landmarks in Orthodontics.
desc: [Healthcare informatics research] This study quantitatively evaluated the accuracy and clinical reliability of EzOrtho, deep learning software designed to identify anatomical landmarks automatically for orthodontic diagnosis. Real-world clinical data were used to assess its applicability in practice. We analyzed 23 lateral cephalometric radiographs. EzOrtho automatically identified 36 anatomical landmarks per radiograph, yielding 828 data points for comparison with ground truth established by experienced orthodontists using a standardized annotation protocol. Accuracy was quantified using mean radial error (MRE), and clinical reliability was assessed using the successful detection rate (SDR), defined as the percentage of all points within the clinically acceptable threshold of 2.0 mm. The overall MRE was 0.78 mm, and the SDR at the 2.0 mm threshold was 86%. Although most landmarks were detected precisely, the landmark-specific analysis identified higher error rates at a few points in anatomically complex regions, indicating areas for improvement. The findings suggest that EzOrtho may offer clinical utility and reliability for automatic cephalometric landmark detection using real clinical data. Its performance indicates the potential to improve efficiency and consistency relative to manual tracing. However, the study's limitations, including its small sample size, mean that these results remain preliminary. Further validation is needed to establish its role as a decision-support tool in orthodontic practice.

title: A Benchmark Protocol and Fairness Analysis Towards Open-Set EEG Seizure Type Classification
desc: Automated EEG seizure type classification systems are typically trained and evaluated under the closed-set assumption, where all seizure types encountered at deployment are seen during training. In clinical practice, this assumption fails: patients present with rare or atypical seizure types that fall outside the training label space, and a system that forces a wrong label is worse than one that abstains. We introduce the first open-set recognition protocol for EEG seizure type classification on the Temple University Hospital Seizure Corpus (TUSZ v2.0.3), defining known and unknown classes using the clinical taxonomy itself: seizure types with sufficient subject representation (at least 12 subjects) form the known set, and rare types form the unknown set. We evaluate seven post-hoc open-set scorers (MSP, MaxLogit, energy, Mahalanobis, kNN, GHOST, and COSTARR) applied to a partially fine-

title: The current state of artificial intelligence and adolescent mental health: the promise and perils of a new frontier.
source: PubMed · Current problems in pediatric and adolescent health care
desc: [Current problems in pediatric and adolescent health care] Adolescent mental health remains a topic of concern in the United States and worldwide. The COVID-19 pandemic accelerated the youth mental health crisis, which began nearly a decade earlier. The ongoing shortage of mental health professionals, including therapists and child and adolescent psychiatrists, means many adolescents who require mental health treatment do not receive it. The emergence of artificial intelligence (AI) technology has demonstrated promise in the field of adolescent mental health, including in screening, detection and risk prediction, intervention and treatment, clinical decision support and workflow augmentation, and in the training of future mental health professionals. However, the study of AI tools in the mental health space remains in its infancy, and most are not yet ready for routine use in clinical practice. Furthermore, the potential risks of AI and its use in adolescent mental health treatment are significant and must be addressed prior to widespread use. Health care professionals, adolescents, and their caregivers need to develop AI literacy to use the technology safely and responsibly. Additionally, AI governance and legal frameworks are necessary to ensure that AI technology use is safe, equitable and ethical for all users. At the present time, AI technology should serve a supportive and complementary role to human-delivered adolescent mental health care.

title: MorphoHELM: A Comprehensive Benchmark for Evaluating Representations for Microscopy-Based Morphology Assays
desc: Microscopy images contain rich information about how cells respond to perturbations, making them essential to applications like drug screening. To quantify images, researchers often use representation extraction methods, and recent years have seen a proliferation of deep learning methods. While measuring the quality of these representations is essential, evaluation remains fragmented, with each proposed model evaluated on different tasks and datasets, using custom pipelines and metrics, making it difficult to fairly compare models. Here, we introduce MorphoHELM, a comprehensive open benchmark for evaluating feature extraction methods for Cell Painting, the most widely-used morphological profiling assay. MorphoHELM consolidates evaluation standards in the field, extends and corrects them to be more robust, and evaluates on the widest range of methods to date. A defining feature of the ben

title: AI-assisted high-throughput screening of MOFs for formaldehyde capture.
desc: [Journal of hazardous materials] Formaldehyde (FA) is a hazardous indoor volatile organic compound that poses risks to human health, demanding efficient adsorbent materials. Functionalized Metal-Organic Frameworks (MOFs) offer structural tunability; however, functionalization can alter the framework, increase heterogeneity, cause pore blockage, and increase cost. Identification of pristine MOFs for FA adsorption is crucial for understanding adsorption mechanisms, framework topology, chemical composition, and unfunctionalized structures. In this work, we present an AI-assisted high-throughput screening framework that combines Generative Artificial Intelligence (GAI)-based text mining, Grand Canonical Monte Carlo (GCMC) simulations, and Machine Learning (ML) to accelerate the discovery of MOFs for FA capture. Four MOF features were extracted using GAI text mining, and 1208 MOFs were selected from the CoRE MOF 2019 database. GCMC simulations evaluated FA uptake, while atomic, geometric, chemical, and thermodynamic descriptors were extracted for ML analyses. Seven regressors were developed to predict FA uptake based on these descriptors. An SVR-based denoising method was introduced during preprocessing to reduce simulation noise and improve predictions. The SVR model showed the best performance with an R² value of 0.94 and predicted FA uptake in 500 hMOFs. Validation of GAI responses, feature analyses, and experimental data also confirmed the reliability of this approach.

title: PathOPEN: A pathologist-curated histopathology dataset for visual question answering
desc: PathOPEN is a histopathology dataset for visual question answering. Two clinical pathologists selected 157 cases with 229 available original images and wrote open-ended, five-option multiple-choice and close-ended (yes/no) questions. They supplied both a correct and a wrong answer for 201 of the 309 open-ended questions. Each case records the organ, pathology category and regional anatomy, and each image records its magnification. The dataset includes 6,870 augmented images and four manifests that select subsets to improve balance by individual metadata field. Five additional pathologists and two vision-language model judges rated items with scoring rubrics, and six models answered questions zero-shot across the three formats. The metadata support subgroup evaluation, and the paired answers can be used to construct preference examples.

title: Machine learning-driven prediction of antimicrobial resistance in Staphylococcus aureus using genomic and allelic signatures.
desc: [Frontiers in microbiology] Antimicrobial resistance (AMR) in Staphylococcus aureus is a growing clinical threat, and machine learning (ML) offers a scalable approach to identifying allele-level resistance determinants. Using a dataset of 300 clinical isolates, we trained and compared seven ML models - LSTM, CNN, Multi-Layer Perceptron (MLP), Decision Tree, XGBoost, Logistic Regression, and Stochastic Gradient Descent (SGD) - to predict resistance across six clinically important antibiotics from allele, locus-tag, and EggNOG-annotation features. Training-set class imbalance was corrected with SMOTE and all seven models were retrained under one identical pipeline. XGBoost achieved the strongest overall test-set performance (accuracy 95%, ROC AUC 0.9745, F1-score 0.9474), closely matched by Decision Tree (accuracy 95%, F1-score 0.9520). Both outperformed the deep-learning architectures (LSTM, CNN, MLP), which showed pronounced overfitting after class-imbalance correction. SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) analysis identified "cat__allele_Cluster_1015_Allele_8" as the most influential feature; this association is hypothesis-generating and reflects statistical importance within this dataset, not a confirmed causal or biological mechanism. The genomic feature set was selected once, on the full isolate collection, by a prior SVM-RFE pipeline before the present train/test split, and no external, temporal, or multi-center validation dataset was used. Reported performance should therefore be read as an upper-bound, best-case estimate rather than a validated benchmark. These findings support ML, and ensemble methods such as XGBoost and Decision Tree in particular, as candidate components of future AMR surveillance and diagnostic pipelines, pending external and prospective validation.

title: EchoAlign: Echocardiography foundation model with multilevel report alignment
desc: Echocardiography assesses the structure and function of the heart. Cardiologists read each study across several standard views and report the findings visible in those views by cardiac structure. AI foundation models can learn to analyze these studies from clinical reports, reducing annotation burden and supporting clinical interpretation. However, existing models are trained by pairing each video with the full clinical report, including structures and findings its view does not show. This mismatch lets a model associate a finding with incidental or spurious signals rather than its visual evidence, which limits accuracy, anatomical grounding and clinical trust. Here we introduce EchoAlign, a vision-language foundation model developed on 2.87 million echocardiographic videos and images from 159 clinical centers. EchoAlign aligns each cardiac structure, video and study with its report text

title: scCont: Interpretable Contrastive Learning for Functional Characterization of Cellular State Transitions.
source: PubMed · bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
desc: [bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology] Timecourse single-cell RNA (scRNA) datasets have become indispensable biological tools for studying and uncovering the underlying regulatory processes driving continuous cell-state transitions such as the epithelial-to-mesenchymal transition. However, these highly fluid, non-linear gene program dynamics remain difficult to disentangle. While deep neural network models can effectively map complex topologies, they are biological black boxes, lacking the gene-level interpretability required by experimental practitioners. Here, we introduce scCont, a fully unsupervised contrastive learning framework for extracting interpretable functional transition units from scRNA-seq data. Rather than relying on explicit temporal labels or clustering priors, scCont uses an unsupervised k-nearest neighbors approach to project local transcriptomic neighborhoods into a low-dimensional embedding. During post-training analysis, scCont employs Shapley network attribution to determine gene-latent relationships, mapping latent dimensions directly into functional gene programs. We quantitatively and qualitatively validate this representation by demonstrating that scCont captures biologically interpretable dynamics more effectively than baseline methods such as LDVAE. Evaluated across 13 diverse EMT timecourse datasets and four simulated datasets, scCont exposes interpretable functional dynamics and effectively maps context-dependent functional groups, helping to bridge the gap between deep learning representation and translational biological utility. scCont is an open source software available on GitHub ( https://github.com/nramani611/scCont ).

title: Towards Clinically Interpretable Ophthalmic VQA via Spatially-Grounded Lesion Evidence
desc: Visual Question Answering (VQA) holds great promise for clinical support, particularly in ophthalmology, where retinal fundus photography is essential for diagnosis. However, ophthalmic VQA benchmarks primarily emphasize answer accuracy, neglecting the explicit visual evidence necessary for clinical interpretability. In this work, we introduce FundusGround, a new benchmark for clinically interpretable ophthalmic VQA with spatially-grounded lesion evidence. Specifically, we propose a three-stage pipeline that collects 10,719 fundus images with 15,595 image-level meticulously annotated lesions. To ensure anatomical consistency and clinical validity, all lesions are spatially localized using the Early Treatment Diabetic Retinopathy Study (ETDRS) grid, enabling standardized mapping to nine clinically meaningful retinal regions. Built upon this structured lesion evidence, 72,706 questions are

title: Long-term tracking of individual pigs through re-identification.
desc: [Smart agricultural technology] Livestock production benefits from automated monitoring of animal health and welfare. However, continuous tracking of commercial pigs using Computer Vision (CV) is hindered by their uniform appearance, the need to avoid reliance on physical tags in commercial settings, and changes in appearance due to growth and dirt. This study addresses longitudinal tracking through an open-set Re-Identification (ReID) framework based on deep metric learning, designed to maintain the identities of visually uniform group-housed pigs without artificial or natural marks. A ResNet50 backbone was fine-tuned with a combined ArcFace and semi-hard triplet loss on a large-scale longitudinal dataset of visually uniform pigs. To mitigate embedding drift, a multi-anchor voting algorithm matched daily cluster centroids against a rolling bank of historical identity representations, while custom synthetic dirt augmentation prevented overfitting to transient dirt patterns. Three modalities were evaluated: Instance Segmentation (IS), Oriented Bounding Boxes (OBB) and Axis-Aligned Bounding Boxes (AABB). During an 18-day open-set evaluation, the multi-anchor framework reached a mean tracking accuracy of 88.0% with IS images, outperforming a sequential day-to-day baseline (54.6%). OBB performance was comparable to IS at lower computational cost, whereas AABB degraded to 51.4%, attributed to background noise. Without synthetic dirt augmentation, tracking fell to 56.5% for IS images. An adapted GradCAM showed consistent attention to body regions such as the head, shoulder and rear, suggesting that identification may rely on stable anatomical traits rather than transient artefacts. These findings indicate that ReID of visually uniform pigs is feasible without physical tags, a step toward non-invasive, continuous welfare monitoring in precision livestock farming.

title: A Multi-Center Dataset and Benchmark for SYNTAX Segmentation of Coronary Angiograms
desc: Dense pixel-level classification of coronary angiography is essential for automated cardiovascular diagnostics, yet the computer vision community lacks gold-standard protocols and robust datasets to tackle this topologically complex, heavily long-tailed domain. To bridge this gap, we introduce CARDIAG: a rigorous, multi-center benchmark dataset designed to evaluate deep learning architectures on fine-grained SYNTAX segment classification. Unlike prior efforts, CARDIAG systematically prevents patient- and center-level data leakage while providing an unprecedented suite of annotations: highly imbalanced multi-class labels, explicit catheter and stenosis masks, expert uncertainty maps, temporal sequence frames, and spatial metadata. Using CARDIAG, we conduct the most extensive architectural sweep in this domain, benchmarking 24 models spanning classic CNNs, Vision Transformers (ViTs), and S

title: Modeling brake wear particle emissions under diverse driving conditions: A data-driven time-series approach.
desc: [Journal of hazardous materials] With the forthcoming Euro 7 regulation, the representativeness of brake particle emissions measured under the WLTP-Brake cycle has received increasing attention. In this study, two pad materials from different vehicles were tested on a brake dynamometer under multiple driving conditions. Although PM10 emissions under the WLTP-Brake cycle complied with the regulatory limit, exceedances occurred under other conditions. Variations in PN emissions among cycles reflected the cumulative effects of preceding brake events, indicating strong temporal dependence. Machine-learning models were therefore developed to predict PN emissions and identify influential brake features. Under time-series inputs, the Transformer achieved the best predictive performance, with an R2 of 0.85 ± 0.03, while XGBoost also showed acceptable accuracy. SHAP analysis showed that high-emission tests were mainly associated with positive contributions from temperature and brake power, whereas low-emission tests were characterized by negative contributions from features such as vehicle speed. Speed was positively related to PN emissions, and brake power amplified its influence. Overall, the proposed approach enables brake particle emissions to be evaluated under diverse driving conditions and may support future brake-emission assessment and regulation.

title: LUCA: A Synthetic World for Experimental Reasoning
desc: An experimental agent can succeed for the wrong reasons. Evaluations, however, often focus on the outcome, not the experiments, evidence, and inferences that produced it. We introduce LUCA, a configurable synthetic world for evaluating this process under fully known ground truth. Agents learn unknown regulatory systems through budgeted experimentation, then predict unseen interventions, diagnose hidden faults, and attempt rescues. This setup allows us to evaluate experiment selection, prediction, diagnosis, and intervention separately. Across seven frontier LLMs and three baselines, these capabilities dissociate sharply. Agents frequently rescue malfunctioning systems while diagnosing the wrong fault; diagnosis varies 7x across models while prediction varies only 1.4x. Models also adopt surprisingly different experimental strategies, and greater exploration does not reliably yield better

title: How Does SAM-3 Adapt? Capacity, Update Geometry, and Domain Transfer
desc: Promptable segmentation foundation models are increasingly used in specialized domains, but it remains unclear how SAM-3 should be fine-tuned when adapting it beyond its original training distribution. We study this question by comparing five adaptation families --LoRA, HiRA, KRAdapter, QuanTA, and Full Fine-Tuning-- across five segmentation datasets spanning medical imaging, remote sensing, and dense material segmentation. Across these datasets, compact parameter-efficient fine-tuning methods often match or approach Full Fine-Tuning in DSC and IoU, suggesting that strong in-domain adaptation does not always require updating the full model. However, this performance cannot be explained by nominal adapter rank or trainable parameter count alone. To investigate why different methods perform similarly, we analyze their update spectra and their behavior under LoveDA Urban/Rural transfer. Our

title: LingSante-Pulse: Unified Physiological Pretraining through Random-Feature Prediction and Cross-Modal Alignment
desc: Clinical monitoring and wearable devices capture complementary physiological signals, but their partially overlapping modality coverage makes within-signal information and cross-modal relationships difficult to exploit jointly. We introduce LingSante-Pulse, a unified, general-purpose and flexible physiological representation framework that learns from these heterogeneous recordings. A shared, signal-conditioned encoder processes each physical channel independently and supports different numbers and combinations of signals for multimodal assessment and single-sensor inference. Pairwise cross-modal alignment, structured random-feature prediction (RFP) and masked waveform reconstruction jointly learn physiological relationships and preserve informative within-signal structure. Across 38 general physiological task configurations spanning PPG, ECG, EEG and EMG, the frozen encoder achieves the

title: TrojanMaxxing: One-shotting VLM Backdoors with Weight-Space Programming
desc: Recent work shows that large language models (LLMs) can reason directly about the weights of other neural networks. Given only a natural-language objective, an LLM can inspect a model's weights, understand what they compute, and edit them directly without gradient-based optimization. This capability, termed weight-space programming (WSP), has been used to improve model performance on math reasoning, medical QA and other benchmarks. We propose TrojanMaxxing, a novel strategy to backdoor vision-language models (VLMs), by reframing it as a WSP task. We use Claude Opus 5.5 and Mythos 5.2 agents to backdoor VLMs without any optimization or training methods. The agents inspect the model weights, apply targeted edits, and co-design an imperceptible visual trigger that activates the backdoor. We then study the agents' strategies and present a thorough evaluation of the trojaned models on various

title: Comparative Performance of Machine Learning Architectures for Fault Detection and Diagnosis in Chemical Processes
desc: Fault Detection and Diagnosis (FDD) is crucial for both maintenance and control in chemical industries, where early fault detection can prevent costly failures and optimize operations. This is particularly critical in pilot units like those at IFP Energies Nouvelles (IFPEN), which operate under short-term experimental conditions with frequently varying operational parameters. This study conducts an extensive benchmarking analysis using the Tennessee Eastman Process (TEP), a widely used simulated chemical process dataset, to evaluate multiple approaches for fault detection and diagnosis, featuring numerous continuous operations with different sensors and faults. Several methods were implemented and compared including Multi Scale PCA (MS-PCA), AutoEncoder, Ensemble Learning, and LSTM models for fault detection, alongside Random Forest, XGBoost, and BLSTM (Bidirectional LSTM) for fault diag

title: Spatiotemporal Graph Neural Networks for Fault Detection and Structural Learning in Chemical Processes: Use Case on the Tennessee Eastman Process
desc: Classical Fault Detection and Diagnosis (FDD) methods, including many data-driven approaches, assume a static normal operating space and interpret deviations from a fixed reference as fault indicators. When Operating Conditions (OCs) vary over time, this assumption breaks down: legitimate transitions trigger false alarms while moderate faults go undetected. We propose a spatiotemporal Graph Neural Network (GNN) framework that decomposes the normal operating space into OC-specific subspaces linked by transition functions, with a dual learning objective combining reconstruction loss and a Deep SVDD one-class term. It learns adjacency matrices through Graph Attention Networks (GATs) and integrates spatial modelling with temporal encoding to represent process dynamics under evolving OCs. This paper evaluates the framework's foundational components (fault detection, GATv2 spatial graph learni

title: SLP-Bench: Evaluating and Improving Acoustic Claims of Reasoning Audio Language Models on Clinical Speech
desc: Audio language models (ALMs) can answer clinical questions from speech, outperforming baselines built on handcrafted acoustic features. Reasoning ALMs generate a chain of thought that refers to properties of the speaker's voice before predicting. Each statement the model makes about the voice needs to be checked against clinicians' perceptual ratings of the same recording. On clinical speech, existing evaluations score only the final answer. We introduce Speech Language Pathologist Bench (SLP-Bench), a benchmark grading each acoustic claim in the chain of thought against clinicians' perceptual ratings of the same recording. It covers five clinician-rated datasets and 25 perceptual dimensions, and assesses claims for factuality, stability under resampling, and consistency across reworded and different questions. Across ten open-weight reasoning ALMs evaluated zero-shot, claim balanced acc

title: TEA-Bench-BR: Can Coding Agents Turn a Branching Clinical Specification into Correct Code?
desc: Coding agents increasingly implement rules written by domain experts, and bugs in such code are silent: it runs and returns a plausible answer. We introduce TEA-Bench-BR, a benchmark built on the Brazilian pathway for early autism (TEA) screening: three fictitious instruments with the structure of real ones, a multi-professional referral flow, and export to FHIR R4 with the national RNDS profiles, all specified in Portuguese. A generator samples each task's parameters (144 tasks, 6,798 hidden cases), and the hidden cases kill all 1,955 non-equivalent mutants of the reference. With Gemma 4 as the agent, the 12B solves 38.0% of single-instrument tasks and none at the FHIR level; the 31B solves 77.8%, 85.2% and 78.7% at levels 1 to 3 and passes over 99% of the hidden cases, its remaining failures mostly in input validation rather than clinical decisions. With the same tasks in English, the

title: ACESO: Cross-Modal Distillation for Wearable-Free Freezing of Gait Detection in Parkinsons Disease
desc: Freezing of Gait (FoG) is a paroxysmal disruption of motor skills and control caused by the progressive decline in the basal ganglia's capacity to produce dopamine. FoG manifests suddenly and without warning. Its detection currently relies on body-worn kinematic sensors called inertial measurement units (IMUs). While IMUs provide the best kinematic precision, the need to wear them severely restricts continuous clinical deployment, both logistically and economically. Vision-based detection removes the sensor but is less accurate. To narrow this gap, we propose a supervised cross-modal subspace distillation framework. During training, we turn the kinematic data from the recorded session and the contextual clinical metadata, together with a textual annotation of the video recordings, into oracles that guide a camera-only freeze detector. Empirical evaluations confirm the validity of our app

title: Towards Text-Mask Consistency in Medical Image Segmentation
desc: Vision-language models for medical image segmentation often produce masks that conflict with the accompanying text, especially under multi-site/multi-lesion descriptions. We trace this failure to two factors: (i) highly templated and repetitive clinical language causes one-to-one hard contrastive learning to yield numerous false negatives, weakening cross-modal alignment; and (ii) predominantly vision-driven, one-way cross-attention lacks a language-dominant, spatially aware pathway, hindering effective injection of textual semantics into the spatial visual domain. To this end, we propose Consistency-enhanced Two-stage Segmentation (C2Seg). In the pretraining stage, Cluster-aware Contrastive Learning uses a frozen strong baseline to construct an intra-batch text similarity matrix as soft labels, thereby alleviating false negative conflicts and producing more discriminative visual represe

title: EgoSurgHands: An Egocentric 3D Hand Pose Dataset & Benchmark for Open Surgery Training
desc: Surgical skill assessment, AR guidance, and robot learning from demonstration all benefit from 3D tracking of the surgeon's hands, yet no surgical dataset offers real egocentric articulated 3D hand pose. We introduce EgoSurgHands, a benchmark for real-captured egocentric hand pose estimation in open surgery training on synthetic pads. Captured with multi-sensor glasses, it contains 41,909 training hand-instance rows across 55 procedure recordings and 9,476 human-validated evaluation rows across 13 held-out recordings, spanning 13 tasks, 3 glove colors, and 4 trainees from first-year medical student to third-year resident. Each frame carries a multi-sensor stack: intrinsics, hand landmarks with per-hand confidence, timestamps, and eye gaze, plus SLAM extrinsics where SLAM succeeded. Evaluation labels combine sensor-fused pseudo-ground truth, human cross-review of every frame, surgeon adju

title: Interpretable Tissue Architecture Complements Pathology Foundation Models
desc: Tissue architecture provides important information for histopathological assessment, yet its complementary predictive value alongside pathology foundation-model representations remains insufficiently understood. This study investigates whether interpretable measurements of cellular and multicellular tissue organization provide additional predictive information beyond learned representations. We introduce a 139-dimensional cellular-to-community representation comprising nine feature groups characterizing nuclear morphology, cellular composition, spatial connectivity, community organization, and cell-cell interactions. Their predictive contributions are systematically evaluated independently and through feature-level fusion with CTransPath and PLIP embeddings using multiple-instance learning (MIL). On the BCNB dataset, estrogen receptor (ER) and progesterone receptor (PR) classification is

title: Stochastic Grouping Conformal Prediction for Effective Subgroup Reliability
desc: Conformal prediction offers a distribution-free coverage guarantee, making it especially attractive for clinical applications. Standard conformal prediction, however, provides such guarantees only at the population level, and its prediction sets can exhibit coverage disparities across clinically important subgroups. A natural remedy is to calibrate within predefined groups. However, this can require access to sensitive subgroup attributes and is prone to a worst-group bottleneck: protecting the most difficult subgroup can inflate prediction sets for all, increasing cognitive burden on decision makers. To this end, we propose Stochastic Grouping Conformal Prediction (SGCP), a conformal framework for subgroup-reliable uncertainty quantification. It learns a stochastic grouping map that allows each sample to draw calibration information from others with similar calibration behavior, yieldin

title: When MLLMs miss what humans read: diagnosing and learning to read squint text
desc: Multimodal LLMs can fail to read text embedded in an image's coarse structure, text a human recovers by squinting, and report that no text is present. We name this class Squint Text and study it as a recognition deficiency, motivated by cases from a production moderation pipeline. We introduce SquintBench, comprising 1076 production-derived moderation images, and SquintCtrl, a controlled synthetic suite for mechanism diagnosis. Frozen-weight analysis shows that hidden text leaves a coarse signal while glyph identity is weakly decodable under global pooling. Restricting read-out to the text region improves glyph-identity decoding, identifying spatial selection as an important factor in glyph-identity read-out; an exact glyph mask further improves decoding. Suppressing high-frequency content also improves reading at a fixed visual-token budget, while visual token count may also contribute.

title: Tracing the Scientific Discovery Capacity of LLMs to Their Training Data
desc: Large language models (LLMs) show growing promise for scientific discovery, yet basic questions remain about what enables reliable discovery. How can we trace the scientific discovery capacity of LLMs to their training data? We study this question as one of missing probability mass and develop a theoretical account in which monofacts---the facts observed once during training---set the discovery capacity. In materials science and regulatory genomics, we directly manipulate monofact rates in training sets and find that more monofacts consistently yield more discoveries across two open-weight model families, sampling strategies, and reasoning budgets. Further experiments show the relationship weakens under miscalibration, cannot be explained by training-set diversity, and can transfer across scientific domains when paired with in-domain data. title: One state, many questions: Opsis gives a frontier model typed eyes for pathology
desc: A synoptic pathology report is a checklist of questions with fixed answer sets, many composed from others. Pathology foundation models answer them accurately with one classifier trained with labels for each, and frontier language models, which compose freely, cannot fit a slide of fourteen thousand tiles in their context. On 189 breast report questions, frontier models that read a written description of the slide or look at a thumbnail and tiles of it answer at 0.50 to 0.66, below the majority class at 0.67. A description is written before the question is known, and a look covers a handful of tiles. We present Opsis, which lets the model ask instead: a typed question interface on a frozen pathology encoder. title: GEG-SAM: Gaze Exploration-Guided Segment Anything Model for Weakly Supervised Polyp Segmentation
desc: Endoscopist gaze offers an unobtrusively acquired record of lesion-oriented visual exploration during routine clinical inspection, providing relevant supervision for tasks. However, existing methods treat fixations as isolated spatial prompts directly associated with the target, overlooking the fact that natural gaze records a continuous visual search process in which fixations are temporally connected, spatially organized, and coupled with the visual content. Interpreting each fixation independently based only on its local visual content overlooks the temporal evolution and spatial organization of the gaze trajectory, whereas modeling relations among fixations alone cannot reveal the visual semantics of the regions they attend to.
