title: Mechanism Parity for Simulation-Based Validation of Autonomous-Driving Perception
desc: Simulation is central to intelligent-vehicle validation, but visual realism or output agreement between a real scene and its synthetic counterpart does not prove that a perception system used the same evidence in both domains. This paper addresses that mechanism-parity gap for paired real-synthetic autonomous-driving perception. It unifies Decisive-Feature Fidelity, which compares decisive evidence maps in a frozen system under test (SUT), with Concept-Decisive Feature Fidelity, which projects decisive evidence into semantic scene concepts for diagnosis. The framework is a validation diagnostic rather than a standalone safety certificate: it asks whether output-consistent simulation also preserves the mechanism by which the perception model reaches that output. title: Progressive Masked Refinement Self-supervised Learning for Low-Dose CT Denoising
desc: Self-supervised learning has been increasingly investigated for low-dose computed tomography (LDCT) image denoising, as it alleviates the dependence on paired normal-dose CT (NDCT) data, which are often difficult to obtain. However, many existing self-supervised blind-spot denoising methods may under-utilize pixel-wise supervisory information due to evaluating the training loss only at masked locations. To address this, we propose a Progressive Masked Refinement Learning framework that recovers NDCT features through iterative refinement with different masking patterns: the denoised output of each step is fed back as the input to the next, so that loss is calculated at a larger proportion of image pixels and the estimate is progressively driven closer to the underlying clean image. title: HistoGPA: A Context-Conditioned Gene-Prior Attention Framework for Histology-Based Spatial Gene Expression Prediction
desc: Spatial transcriptomics is costly, motivating the prediction of spatial gene expression from routine hematoxylin and eosin (H&E) slides. Existing methods use tissue context to refine visual features but keep pretrained gene priors fixed across specimens. Since the relevance of such a prior may vary with tissue context, we propose HistoGPA, which conditions the gene prior itself on the slide being analyzed. A slide-level histological representation modulates a memory of pretrained gene embeddings before each spatial location queries it through cross-attention, and also gates context into the local features. Across ten cancer-specific tasks from HEST-1k, HistoGPA achieves a macro-averaged gene-wise Pearson correlation of 0.300 on the HEST-Bench genes, compared with 0.260 for the strongest of four recent methods. title: Segment Everything, Materialize Nothing: Exact Streaming Inference for Many-Class 3D Segmentation
desc: Whole-body segmentation tools such as TotalSegmentator and MOOSE split more than 100 classes across five or six networks. The reason is memory. Standard 3D inference, as implemented in nnU-Net and MONAI, holds a logit for every class and voxel, on the working grid and again on the scanner's grid. For a median whole-body CT at 125 classes, that is 76 GB. We show that this memory wall lies in what inference materializes, not in the task, and remove it without approximation. Every step after the network is local along one axis, so its outputs can be streamed through a ring one patch thick. The classification head commutes with blending and resampling, so the ring carries the network's features instead of the class logits. title: Saddle Buckling of a Multicellular Alga Driven by Differential Growth
desc: During development of many simple multicellular organisms there is a complex interplay between cell growth and generation of an extracellular matrix that confers structure. We study this problem quantitatively using $Gonium~pectorale$, a 16-cell alga that transforms from a flat to a buckled shape during growth without cell division or rearrangement. Cell-level measurements and 3D reconstructions show that the $12$ peripheral cells grow faster than the central $4$, producing hoop stress that selects the saddle mode, whose amplitude displays a continuous bifurcation with classical square root singularity. These results are consistent with a continuum model of differential growth within Föppl--von Kármán theory, which yields information on the mechanical properties of the ECM. Implications of this transformation in evolutionary transitions to multicellularity are discussed.
